source.text: Μὴ πολλοὶ διδάσκαλοι γίνεσθε, ἀδελφοί μου, εἰδότες ὅτι μεῖζον κρίμα λημψόμεθα·

records.literal_gloss: Not many teachers become, brothers of me, knowing that greater judgment we will receive;

en.L: Not many [of you] should become teachers, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.
en.B: Not many of you should become teachers, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, for you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, not many of you should become teachers. You know that we teachers will be judged more strictly than others.

es.L: No {{plural_you:se hagan|os hagáis}} maestros muchos [de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}], hermanos míos, sabiendo que recibiremos un juicio mayor.
es.B: No {{plural_you:deberían|deberíais}} hacerse maestros muchos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos míos, pues {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que los que enseñamos recibiremos un juicio más estricto.
es.R: Hermanos míos, no muchos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} ser maestros. {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} que a nosotros, los maestros, se nos juzgará con más rigor que a los demás.

sw.L: Wengi [wenu] wasiwe walimu, ndugu zangu, mkijua kwamba sisi tutapokea hukumu iliyo kubwa zaidi.
sw.B: Ndugu zangu, wengi wenu wasiwe walimu, kwa maana mnajua kwamba sisi tunaofundisha tutahukumiwa kwa kipimo kikali zaidi.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, si wengi wenu wanaopaswa kuwa walimu. Mnajua kwamba sisi walimu tutahukumiwa kwa ukali zaidi kuliko wengine.

fr.L: Ne soyez pas nombreux à devenir enseignants, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, sachant que nous recevrons un jugement plus grand.
fr.B: Ne soyez pas nombreux à devenir enseignants, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, car vous savez que nous qui enseignons, nous serons jugés plus sévèrement.
fr.R: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, peu d’entre vous devraient devenir enseignants. Vous savez que nous, les enseignants, nous serons jugés plus sévèrement que les autres.

ko.L: 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분 가운데 많은 사람이 선생이 되지 마십시오. 우리가 더 큰 심판을 받을 것을 알기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분 가운데 많은 사람이 선생이 되려고 하지 마십시오. 여러분도 알다시피, 가르치는 우리는 더 엄격한 심판을 받을 것입니다.
ko.R: 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분 가운데 많은 사람이 가르치는 사람이 되려고 해서는 안 됩니다. 여러분도 알다시피, 우리 가르치는 사람들은 다른 사람들보다 더 엄격하게 심판을 받을 것입니다.

vi.L: Chớ có nhiều [người trong anh chị em] trở thành người dạy dỗ, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, vì biết rằng chúng ta sẽ chịu sự phán xét nghiêm khắc hơn.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, không nên có nhiều người trong anh chị em làm người dạy dỗ, vì anh chị em biết rằng chúng ta, những người dạy dỗ, sẽ bị phán xét nghiêm khắc hơn.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, không nên có nhiều người trong anh chị em trở thành người dạy dỗ. Anh chị em biết rằng chúng tôi, những người dạy dỗ, sẽ bị phán xét nghiêm khắc hơn những người khác.

pt.L: Não se tornem muitos [de vocês] mestres, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, sabendo que receberemos um julgamento maior.
pt.B: Não sejam muitos de vocês mestres, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, pois vocês sabem que nós, que ensinamos, seremos julgados com mais rigor.
pt.R: Meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, poucos de vocês devem se tornar mestres. Vocês sabem que nós, os mestres, seremos julgados com mais rigor do que os outros.

am.L: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ የበለጠ ፍርድ እንደምንቀበል እያወቃችሁ ብዙዎቻችሁ መምህራን አትሁኑ።
am.B: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ ብዙዎቻችሁ መምህራን አትሁኑ፤ እኛ የምናስተምር ይበልጥ በጥብቅ እንደሚፈረድብን ታውቃላችሁና።
am.R: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ ብዙዎቻችሁ አስተማሪዎች መሆን የለባችሁም። እኛ አስተማሪዎች ከሌሎች ይበልጥ በጥብቅ እንደሚፈረድብን ታውቃላችሁ።

decisions.choice: teachers: those who taught the congregation, a recognized role
alternatives: anyone who gives advice or opinions
decisions.reason: Teachers had a named place in the early churches, next to prophets (Acts 13:1; 1 Corinthians 12:28). διδάσκαλοι here means that role. James is not telling believers to stop speaking about God, but warning against rushing to take a teaching role.

decisions.choice: we will receive: James counts himself among the teachers
decisions.reason: The verb changes from "you" to "we": λημψόμεθα. James is a teacher himself, and he puts himself under the same stricter judgment. The "we" of verse 2 ("we all stumble") then widens to everyone.

decisions.choice: a greater judgment: God judges teachers by a stricter standard
decisions.reason: κρίμα is the judgment God passes, and μεῖζον means greater or stricter. Those who teach others are answerable for their words (Matthew 12:36-37) and for what they have been given (Luke 12:48). Verse 2 gives the reason: everyone stumbles, and the teacher's tool is the tongue.

decisions.choice: my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Gender setting: James addresses the whole congregation, women and men.

decisions.choice: we who teach; we teachers
alternatives: we will receive a greater judgment
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the "we" explicit (m2) and say what a greater judgment means for the one judged.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: As in James's other chapters, each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (the default) or vosotros. Where "muchos de ustedes" is the subject, the vosotros form also takes the second-person verb ("os hagáis", "deberíais"), as Spain says it.

decisions.choice: hermanos míos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans: "hermanos" already includes the sisters, so Spanish has no gender span on it in this chapter.

decisions.choice: ndugu zangu, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans: "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili has no gender span in this chapter.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} and the other settings as set out in 1:1, 1:2 and 1:5 (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: The settings of chapters 1 and 2 hold through chapter 3.

decisions.choice: enseignants
decisions.reason: The word names those who taught the congregation (m1). French "maître" today first suggests a master or a schoolteacher of young children, and "docteur" a physician; "enseignant" says the role plainly.

decisions.choice: "선생" (L, B); "가르치는 사람" (R); "우리" with James among the teachers
decisions.reason: The teachers had a recognized role in the congregation (meaning decision); "선생" is the ordinary church word for one who teaches, while "교사" suggests a school. The meaning decision says James counts himself among them, which Korean keeps with "우리".

decisions.choice: "chúng ta" (L, B), "chúng tôi" (R) for "we will receive"
decisions.reason: James counts himself among the teachers (m2). Literal and Balanced keep the inclusive "chúng ta" of the Greek, which speaks to all who might teach; Readable, which names "we teachers" as the English Readable does, uses the exclusive "chúng tôi", since the group is the teachers, not every reader.

decisions.choice: mestres
decisions.reason: The word names the recognized role of teaching in the church (m1). "Professor" in Brazil is a school or university teacher; "mestre" is the word for one who teaches others the way of God.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
alternatives: a span like the English {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in verse 9
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change; pronouns for God are written plainly through the chapter.

source.text: πολλὰ γὰρ πταίομεν ἅπαντες.

records.literal_gloss: In many [ways] for stumble all.

en.L: For we all stumble in many [ways].
en.B: For all of us stumble in many ways.
en.R: All of us stumble and do wrong in many ways.

es.L: Porque en muchas [cosas] tropezamos todos.
es.B: Pues todos tropezamos de muchas maneras.
es.R: Todos tropezamos y fallamos de muchas maneras.

sw.L: Kwa maana tunajikwaa sote kwa [njia] nyingi.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa sisi sote tunajikwaa kwa namna nyingi.
sw.R: Sisi sote tunajikwaa na kukosea kwa njia nyingi.

fr.L: Car nous trébuchons tous de bien des [manières].
fr.B: Car nous trébuchons tous de bien des manières.
fr.R: Nous trébuchons tous et nous faisons le mal de bien des façons.

ko.L: 우리는 모두 여러 가지로 걸려 넘어지기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 우리는 모두 여러 가지로 걸려 넘어집니다.
ko.R: 우리는 모두 여러 가지로 걸려 넘어지고 잘못을 저지릅니다.

vi.L: Vì tất cả chúng ta đều vấp phạm nhiều [cách].
vi.B: Vì tất cả chúng ta đều vấp ngã trong nhiều điều.
vi.R: Tất cả chúng ta đều vấp ngã và làm sai trong nhiều việc.

pt.L: Pois todos tropeçamos em muitas [coisas].
pt.B: Pois todos nós tropeçamos de muitas maneiras.
pt.R: Todos nós tropeçamos e erramos de muitas maneiras.

am.L: ሁላችንም በብዙ ነገር እንሰናከላለንና።
am.B: ሁላችንም በብዙ መንገድ እንሰናከላለንና።
am.R: ሁላችንም በብዙ መንገድ እንሰናከላለን፤ ስሕተትም እንሠራለን።

decisions.choice: stumble: fail, do wrong
decisions.reason: πταίω pictures tripping, and James uses it for failing to keep God's law: one who stumbles in one point is guilty of all (2:10). Here it means any wrongdoing, and verse 2 goes on to the wrongs done in speech.

decisions.choice: in many ways
decisions.reason: πολλὰ is used as an adverb. It can mean "in many respects" or "many times"; both say that no one escapes it. James includes himself in "we all".

decisions.choice: stumble and do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture and says what it means (m1).

source.text: εἴ τις ἐν λόγῳ οὐ πταίει, οὗτος τέλειος ἀνήρ, δυνατὸς χαλιναγωγῆσαι καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone in word does not stumble, this one [is a] perfect man, able to bridle also the whole the body.

en.L: If anyone does not stumble in word, this one [is] a perfect {{gender:person|man}}, able to bridle the whole body as well.
en.B: Anyone who does not stumble in what {{gender:they say|he says}} is a perfect {{gender:person|man}}, able to keep the whole body in check as well.
en.R: Suppose someone never stumbles in what {{gender:they say|he says}}. That person is complete and mature. {{gender:They|He}} can also control {{gender:their|his}} whole body, the way a rider controls a horse with a bridle.

es.L: Si alguno no tropieza en palabra, este [es] {{gender:una persona perfecta|un hombre perfecto}}, capaz de poner freno también a todo el cuerpo.
es.B: Quien no tropieza en lo que dice es {{gender:una persona perfecta|un hombre perfecto}}, capaz de tener a raya también todo su cuerpo.
es.R: Imaginemos a alguien que nunca tropieza en lo que dice. Esa persona es completa y madura. Puede dominar también todo su cuerpo, como un jinete domina a su caballo con el freno.

sw.L: Kama mtu hajikwai katika neno, huyo [ni] mtu kamili, anayeweza kuutia lijamu hata mwili wote.
sw.B: Yeyote asiyejikwaa katika anayoyasema ni mtu kamili, anayeweza pia kuudhibiti mwili wake wote.
sw.R: Tuseme kuna mtu ambaye hajikwai kamwe katika maneno yake. Mtu huyo amekamilika na amekomaa. Anaweza pia kuutawala mwili wake wote, kama mpanda farasi anavyomwongoza farasi kwa lijamu.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un ne trébuche pas en parole, celui-là [est] {{gender:un être humain accompli|un homme accompli}}, capable de tenir en bride aussi le corps tout entier.
fr.B: Celui qui ne trébuche pas dans ce qu’il dit est {{gender:quelqu’un de mûr|un homme mûr}}, capable de maîtriser aussi tout son corps.
fr.R: Imaginons quelqu’un qui ne trébuche jamais dans ce qu’il dit. Celui-là est mûr et complet. Il peut aussi maîtriser tout son corps, comme un cavalier maîtrise son cheval avec une bride.

ko.L: 누구든지 말에 걸려 넘어지지 않으면, 이 사람은 온전한 사람이고, 온몸도 재갈 물려 다스릴 수 있습니다.
ko.B: 말에 걸려 넘어지지 않는 사람은 온전한 사람이며, 온몸도 잘 다스릴 수 있습니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 말로 한 번도 실수하지 않는다고 생각해 보십시오. 그 사람은 다 자란 온전한 사람입니다. 말을 탄 사람이 재갈로 말을 부리듯, 그는 자기 온몸도 다스릴 수 있습니다.

vi.L: Nếu ai không vấp phạm trong lời nói, người ấy là người trọn vẹn, có thể kìm cương cả thân thể nữa.
vi.B: Ai không vấp ngã trong lời nói là người trọn vẹn, có thể chế ngự được cả thân thể mình.
vi.R: Giả sử có người không bao giờ vấp ngã trong lời nói. Người ấy là người trọn vẹn và trưởng thành. Người ấy cũng có thể điều khiển cả thân thể mình, như người cưỡi ngựa dùng dây cương điều khiển con ngựa.

pt.L: Se alguém não tropeça no falar, esse [é] {{gender:uma pessoa perfeita|um homem perfeito}}, capaz de refrear também o corpo inteiro.
pt.B: Quem não tropeça no que diz é {{gender:uma pessoa perfeita|um homem perfeito}}, capaz de manter também todo o corpo sob controle.
pt.R: Imaginem alguém que nunca tropeça no que diz. Essa pessoa é madura e completa. Ela consegue controlar também o corpo inteiro, como o cavaleiro controla o cavalo com o freio.

am.L: ማንም በቃል የማይሰናከል ቢኖር፣ እርሱ መላ ሰውነቱን ደግሞ በልጓም ሊገታ የሚችል ፍጹም ሰው ነው።
am.B: በሚናገረው የማይሰናከል ሰው ፍጹም ሰው ነው፤ መላ ሰውነቱንም ሊቆጣጠር ይችላል።
am.R: አንድ ሰው በሚናገረው ፈጽሞ አይሰናከልም እንበል። ያ ሰው ሙሉና የበሰለ ነው። ጋላቢ ፈረሱን በልጓም እንደሚቆጣጠር እርሱም መላ ሰውነቱን ሊቆጣጠር ይችላል።

decisions.choice: in word: in what one says
decisions.reason: In 1:18-23 λόγος was the word of truth from God. Here, with "stumble", it is a person's own speech, the subject of the whole chapter (verses 5-12).

decisions.choice: perfect: complete, fully mature, not sinless
decisions.reason: τέλειος is the word of 1:4 ("perfect and complete, lacking nothing"). James has just said that everyone stumbles, so he does not mean anyone is free of all sin. He means a person whose speech is so governed that the rest of life is governed too.

decisions.choice: bridle: guide and restrain, as a rider does a horse
decisions.reason: χαλιναγωγῆσαι means to lead with a bridle. James used it in 1:26 for bridling the tongue, and verse 3 develops the picture: the small bit turns the whole horse. Whoever governs the tongue can govern the whole self.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: ἀνήρ usually means a man, but here it takes up "anyone" (τις) and speaks of any believer, so the gender setting applies. The pronouns for that person follow it.

decisions.choice: complete and mature; the way a rider controls a horse with a bridle
decisions.reason: Readable says what "perfect" means here (m2) and spells out the bridle picture, which verse 3 is about to use.

decisions.choice: {{gender:una persona perfecta|un hombre perfecto}}; no span on the pronouns
decisions.reason: Spanish carries the subject in the verb ("puede") and "su" is the same for a man or a woman, so only the noun phrase for ἀνήρ takes the gender setting. Readable's "esa persona" fits both readings.

decisions.choice: mtu, no setting
decisions.reason: "Mtu" is any person, man or woman, so the gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili, and the verbs carry no gendered pronoun.

decisions.choice: kuutia lijamu (L); kwa lijamu (R)
decisions.reason: "Lijamu" is the bit, the part of the bridle that goes into the mouth, and it is the word verse 3 needs. Using it here in Literal and Readable keeps James's link between bridling the body and the bit in the horse's mouth.

decisions.choice: {{gender:un être humain accompli|un homme accompli}} (L); {{gender:quelqu’un de mûr|un homme mûr}} (B); no span at R
decisions.reason: The Greek has "man" in the sense of anyone. The adjective goes inside the span with the noun. "Accompli" (L) and "mûr" (B) are the words chosen for "perfect" in 1:4: complete, fully mature, not sinless (m2). Readable refers back to "quelqu’un" with the inclusive "celui-là".

decisions.choice: "온전한 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek word for "man" here means anyone (the meaning decision reads "perfect" as mature, not as a male); Korean "사람" already includes men and women.

decisions.choice: refrear (L); controlar ... com o freio (R)
decisions.reason: "Freio" is the Brazilian word for a horse's bit and bridle, so "refrear" and "freio" keep the one picture that runs from 1:26 into 3:3 (m3).

decisions.choice: ሰው (person) and the generic masculine suffix, with no gender span, through the chapter
decisions.reason: "ሰው" already means a human being of either sex, and the masculine suffix used of "anyone" includes women, so a second option would read the same. Spans are kept for adelphoi, "brothers".

decisions.choice: ሰውነት (body), and ክፍሎች (parts) for the members, through the chapter
alternatives: ሥጋ (flesh, also used for the body)
decisions.reason: As in Romans, "ሰውነት" is kept for the physical body and "ሥጋ" for flesh; the members are "ክፍሎች" at every level (style brief section 7b).

source.text: εἰ δὲ τῶν ἵππων τοὺς χαλινοὺς εἰς τὰ στόματα βάλλομεν εἰς τὸ πείθεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα αὐτῶν μετάγομεν.

records.literal_gloss: If now of the horses the bits into the mouths we put for the to obey them us, also the whole the body of them we turn.

en.L: Now if we put the bits into the mouths of horses so that they obey us, we also turn their whole body.
en.B: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we steer their whole body as well.
en.R: We put a small bit in the mouth of a horse to make it obey us. Then we can turn its whole body.

es.L: Ahora bien, si ponemos los frenos en las bocas de los caballos para que nos obedezcan, dirigimos también todo su cuerpo.
es.B: Cuando les ponemos el freno en la boca a los caballos para que nos obedezcan, conducimos también todo su cuerpo.
es.R: Le ponemos un pequeño freno en la boca al caballo para que nos obedezca. Así podemos hacer girar todo su cuerpo.

sw.L: Basi ikiwa tunatia lijamu katika vinywa vya farasi ili watutii, tunaugeuza pia mwili wao wote.
sw.B: Tunapotia lijamu vinywani mwa farasi ili watutii, tunauelekeza pia mwili wao wote.
sw.R: Tunatia lijamu ndogo kinywani mwa farasi ili atutii. Ndipo tunaweza kuugeuza mwili wake wote.

fr.L: Or si nous mettons les mors dans la bouche des chevaux pour qu’ils nous obéissent, nous dirigeons aussi tout leur corps.
fr.B: Quand nous mettons un mors dans la bouche des chevaux pour qu’ils nous obéissent, nous dirigeons aussi tout leur corps.
fr.R: Nous mettons un petit mors dans la bouche d’un cheval pour qu’il nous obéisse. Alors nous pouvons faire tourner tout son corps.

ko.L: 우리가 말들을 우리에게 순종하게 하려고 그 입에 재갈을 물리면, 그 온몸도 이끌게 됩니다.
ko.B: 우리는 말을 순종하게 하려고 그 입에 재갈을 물려서, 그 온몸을 원하는 대로 이끕니다.
ko.R: 우리는 말을 순종하게 하려고 말의 입에 작은 재갈을 물립니다. 그러면 말의 온몸을 원하는 쪽으로 돌릴 수 있습니다.

vi.L: Nếu chúng ta đặt hàm thiếc vào miệng ngựa để chúng vâng phục chúng ta, thì chúng ta cũng xoay được cả thân mình chúng.
vi.B: Khi chúng ta đặt hàm thiếc vào miệng ngựa để bắt chúng vâng lời, chúng ta điều khiển được cả thân mình chúng.
vi.R: Chúng ta đặt một cái hàm thiếc nhỏ vào miệng con ngựa để bắt nó vâng lời. Rồi chúng ta có thể xoay cả thân mình nó.

pt.L: Ora, se colocamos os freios na boca dos cavalos para eles nos obedecerem, conduzimos também todo o corpo deles.
pt.B: Quando pomos freios na boca dos cavalos para que nos obedeçam, conduzimos também o corpo inteiro deles.
pt.R: Nós colocamos um pequeno freio na boca do cavalo para que ele nos obedeça. Assim podemos virar o corpo inteiro dele.

am.L: እንዲታዘዙልን በፈረሶች አፍ ልጓም ብናስገባ፣ መላ ሰውነታቸውን ደግሞ እናዞራለን።
am.B: ፈረሶች እንዲታዘዙልን በአፋቸው ልጓም ስናስገባ፣ መላ ሰውነታቸውን እንመራለን።
am.R: ፈረስ እንዲታዘዘን በአፉ ትንሽ ልጓም እናስገባለን። ከዚያም መላ ሰውነቱን ወደምንፈልገው ማዞር እንችላለን።

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "now if"
alternatives: "look", calling attention, as at the start of verse 4
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, including the text behind the King James Version, have a word meaning "look" here, which sounds almost the same as εἰ δὲ and matches ἰδοὺ in verse 4. The SBLGNT reads "now if". The picture and its point do not change. This note is written from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: if: a plain fact used as a comparison
decisions.reason: James is not doubting that riders bridle horses. The "if" states something everyone knows, to compare it with the tongue (verse 5). The "whole body" picks up the end of verse 2.

decisions.choice: bits: the metal mouthpiece of a bridle
decisions.reason: χαλινός can mean the bridle as a whole, but put "into the mouths" it is the bit, the small piece the reins pull on. Its smallness is the point (verses 4-5).

decisions.choice: a small bit
decisions.reason: Readable adds "small" to make clear the point the comparison is making (verse 5).

decisions.choice: freno
decisions.reason: In Spanish "freno" is first of all the bit, the iron piece in a horse's mouth (m3), and it is the noun behind "poner freno" in verse 2 and "refrenar". Keeping it at every level keeps James's link between the two verses.

decisions.choice: "hàm thiếc" for the bits, with "kìm cương" for bridle (1:26; 3:2)
decisions.reason: The bit is the metal mouthpiece of the bridle (m3); "hàm thiếc" is its Vietnamese name, and "kìm cương" (to rein in) keeps James's picture of the rider in 1:26 and 3:2.

source.text: ἰδοὺ καὶ τὰ πλοῖα, τηλικαῦτα ὄντα καὶ ὑπὸ ἀνέμων σκληρῶν ἐλαυνόμενα, μετάγεται ὑπὸ ἐλαχίστου πηδαλίου ὅπου ἡ ὁρμὴ τοῦ εὐθύνοντος βούλεται·

records.literal_gloss: Look also the ships, so great being and by winds hard being driven, are turned by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the [one] steering wants;

en.L: Look also at the ships: though they are so large and are driven by hard winds, they are turned by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the one steering wishes.
en.B: Or look at ships. They are so large, and fierce winds drive them, yet a very small rudder turns them wherever the pilot means to go.
en.R: Or think about ships. They are very big, and strong winds push them along. But a very small rudder turns them wherever the pilot wants to go.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} también los barcos: aunque son tan grandes y son empujados por vientos fuertes, son dirigidos por un timón muy pequeño adonde quiere el impulso del que pilota.
es.B: O {{plural_you:piensen|pensad}} en los barcos. Son tan grandes, y vientos violentos los empujan; sin embargo, un timón muy pequeño los hace girar hacia donde el piloto se propone ir.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} también en los barcos. Son muy grandes, y los vientos fuertes los llevan. Pero un timón muy pequeño los hace girar hacia donde el piloto quiere ir.

sw.L: Tazama pia meli: ingawa ni kubwa kiasi hicho na zinasukumwa na pepo kali, zinageuzwa na usukani mdogo kabisa popote unapotaka msukumo wa yule anayeziongoza.
sw.B: Au fikirini meli. Ni kubwa mno, na upepo mkali huzisukuma, lakini usukani mdogo sana huzigeuza kuelekea popote anapokusudia kwenda yule anayeziongoza.
sw.R: Au fikirini juu ya meli. Ni kubwa sana, na upepo mkali huzisukuma. Lakini usukani mdogo sana huzigeuza kwenda popote anapotaka kwenda yule anayeziongoza.

fr.L: Voyez aussi les navires : bien qu’ils soient si grands et poussés par des vents violents, ils sont dirigés par un tout petit gouvernail là où le veut l’impulsion de celui qui tient la barre ;
fr.B: Voyez aussi les bateaux. Ils sont si grands, et des vents violents les poussent ; pourtant un tout petit gouvernail les dirige là où le pilote veut aller.
fr.R: Pensez aussi aux bateaux. Ils sont très grands, et des vents forts les poussent. Mais un tout petit gouvernail les fait tourner là où le pilote veut aller.

ko.L: 보십시오, 배들도 그렇게 크고 거센 바람에 밀려가는데도, 아주 작은 키로 조종하는 사람의 뜻대로 어디로든지 방향을 돌립니다.
ko.B: 배를 보십시오. 배는 그렇게 크고 거센 바람에 밀려가지만, 아주 작은 키 하나로 사공이 가려는 곳으로 방향을 돌립니다.
ko.R: 배를 생각해 보십시오. 배는 아주 크고, 센 바람이 배를 밀어 갑니다. 그러나 아주 작은 키 하나로 배를 모는 사람이 가고 싶은 곳으로 배를 돌립니다.

vi.L: Hãy xem các con tàu nữa: dù lớn như thế và bị gió mạnh đẩy đi, chúng vẫn được một bánh lái rất nhỏ xoay về bất cứ nơi nào ý muốn của người cầm lái định hướng.
vi.B: Hoặc hãy xem các con tàu. Chúng to lớn như vậy, lại bị gió mạnh đẩy đi, thế mà một bánh lái rất nhỏ cũng xoay chúng về bất cứ hướng nào người lái tàu muốn đi.
vi.R: Hoặc hãy nghĩ về các con tàu. Chúng rất to, và gió mạnh đẩy chúng đi. Nhưng một bánh lái rất nhỏ có thể xoay chúng về bất cứ nơi nào người lái tàu muốn đi.

pt.L: Vejam também os navios: embora sejam tão grandes e levados por ventos fortes, são virados por um leme muito pequeno para onde quer que o impulso de quem os dirige deseje.
pt.B: Ou vejam os navios. São tão grandes, e ventos violentos os empurram; mesmo assim, um leme muito pequeno os faz virar para onde o piloto quer ir.
pt.R: Ou pensem nos navios. Eles são muito grandes, e ventos fortes os empurram. Mas um leme bem pequeno faz o navio virar para onde o piloto quer ir.

am.L: እነሆ፣ መርከቦችም ደግሞ ይህን ያህል ታላላቅ ቢሆኑና በብርቱ ነፋስ ቢነዱም፣ የሚመራቸው ሰው ፍላጎት ወደ ወደደበት በጣም ትንሽ በሆነ መሪ ይዞራሉ።
am.B: መርከቦችንም ተመልከቱ፤ እጅግ ትልልቅ ናቸው፤ ኃይለኛ ነፋስም ይገፋቸዋል፤ ቢሆንም መርከበኛው ሊሄድ ወደ ፈለገበት በጣም ትንሽ መሪ ያዞራቸዋል።
am.R: ወይም ስለ መርከቦች አስቡ። በጣም ትልልቅ ናቸው፤ ብርቱ ነፋስም ይገፋቸዋል። ነገር ግን በጣም ትንሽ የሆነ መሪ መርከበኛው ሊሄድ ወደ ፈለገበት ያዞራቸዋል።

decisions.choice: look: a call to notice the example
decisions.reason: ἰδοὺ calls for attention to a new picture. James uses it again in verse 5 and in chapter 5 (5:4, 5:7, 5:9, 5:11).

decisions.choice: though they are so large and driven by strong winds
decisions.reason: The two participles ὄντα and ἐλαυνόμενα describe the ships in a way that sets up a contrast: large and driven by strong forces, and yet steered by a tiny thing.

decisions.choice: the impulse of the one steering: the pilot's will, where he means to go
alternatives: the push of the pilot's hand on the tiller
decisions.reason: ὁρμὴ means a strong urge or intention. The point is that the will of one person directs the whole ship through the small rudder, as the tongue directs a life.

decisions.choice: wherever the pilot means to go; wherever the pilot wants to go
alternatives: wherever the impulse of the one steering wishes
decisions.reason: The participle εὐθύνοντος is "the one steering", the pilot. Balanced and Readable name him and turn "impulse" into what he means or wants.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}; {{plural_you:piensen|pensad}}
decisions.reason: ἰδοὺ is a fixed call to look. Spanish says it with an imperative, and since James is speaking to his readers the imperative is plural and takes the ustedes / vosotros setting. "He aquí" would avoid the setting but is old-fashioned. The same holds in verse 5.

decisions.choice: "키" for the rudder; "조종하는 사람" (L); "사공" (B); "배를 모는 사람" (R) for the pilot
decisions.reason: "키" is the plain Korean word for a ship's rudder. The one steering is the helmsman, not the owner or captain; "사공" is the familiar word for one who steers a boat.

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα μικρὸν μέλος ἐστὶν καὶ μεγάλα αὐχεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: So also the tongue a small member is and great things boasts.

en.L: So also the tongue is a small member, and it boasts great things.
en.B: In the same way the tongue is a small part of the body, yet it boasts of great things.
en.R: The tongue is like that. It is a small part of the body, but it brags about big things.

es.L: Así también la lengua es un miembro pequeño, y presume de cosas grandes.
es.B: De igual manera, la lengua es una parte pequeña del cuerpo, y sin embargo alardea de cosas grandes.
es.R: Con la lengua pasa lo mismo. Es una parte pequeña del cuerpo, pero presume de cosas muy grandes.

sw.L: Hivyo pia ulimi ni kiungo kidogo, na unajisifu mambo makubwa.
sw.B: Kwa namna hiyohiyo, ulimi ni sehemu ndogo ya mwili, lakini unajigamba kwa mambo makubwa.
sw.R: Ndivyo ulivyo ulimi. Ni sehemu ndogo ya mwili, lakini unajivunia mambo makubwa.

fr.L: Ainsi aussi la langue est un petit membre, et elle se vante de grandes choses.
fr.B: De même, la langue est une petite partie du corps, et pourtant elle se vante de grandes choses.
fr.R: La langue, c’est pareil. C’est une petite partie du corps, mais elle se vante de grandes choses.

ko.L: 이와 같이 혀도 작은 지체이지만 큰 것들을 자랑합니다.
ko.B: 이와 같이 혀도 몸의 작은 부분이지만 큰일을 자랑합니다.
ko.R: 혀도 그와 같습니다. 혀는 몸의 작은 부분이지만 큰일을 할 수 있다고 큰소리칩니다.

vi.L: Cũng vậy, cái lưỡi là một chi thể nhỏ, mà khoe khoang những điều lớn lao.
vi.B: Cũng thế, cái lưỡi là một bộ phận nhỏ của thân thể, nhưng lại khoe khoang những điều lớn lao.
vi.R: Cái lưỡi cũng như vậy. Nó là một bộ phận nhỏ của thân thể, nhưng lại khoác lác những chuyện to tát.

pt.L: Assim também a língua é um pequeno membro e se gloria de grandes coisas.
pt.B: Do mesmo modo, a língua é uma pequena parte do corpo, mas se orgulha de grandes coisas.
pt.R: A língua é assim. Ela é uma pequena parte do corpo, mas se gaba de coisas grandes.

am.L: እንዲሁም ምላስ ትንሽ ክፍል ነው፤ በታላላቅ ነገሮችም ይመካል።
am.B: እንደዚሁም ምላስ ትንሽ የሰውነት ክፍል ነው፤ ነገር ግን በታላላቅ ነገሮች ይመካል።
am.R: ምላስም እንደዚሁ ነው። ትንሽ የሰውነት ክፍል ነው፤ ነገር ግን ስለ ትልልቅ ነገሮች ጉራውን ይነዛል።

decisions.choice: member: a part of the body
decisions.reason: μέλος is a limb or organ. James speaks of the body and its members again in verse 6 and in 4:1.

decisions.choice: boasts great things: makes great claims, and has great power to match
decisions.reason: αὐχεῖ is to boast. Set beside the bit and the rudder, it means that this small part speaks big and sets big things in motion, for good or harm. The next sentence turns to the harm.

decisions.choice: a small part of the body
decisions.reason: "Member" no longer means a part of the body for most readers.

decisions.choice: "지체" (L); "몸의 작은 부분" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "지체" is the word for a part of the body (meaning decision) and links with "우리 지체들" in verse 6; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

decisions.choice: "chi thể" (L); "bộ phận" (B, R) for member, here and in 3:6
decisions.reason: "Chi thể" is the church word for a member of the body, which Literal keeps as the Vietnamese Romans does (12:4); Balanced and Readable say "bộ phận", as the English says "part of the body".

source.text: Ἰδοὺ ἡλίκον πῦρ ἡλίκην ὕλην ἀνάπτει·

records.literal_gloss: Look how small a fire how great a forest sets ablaze;

en.L: Look how small a fire sets ablaze how great a forest!
en.B: Look how small a flame can set so large a forest on fire!
en.R: Just think about it. A tiny flame can set a whole big forest on fire.

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} qué fuego tan pequeño incendia qué bosque tan grande!
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} cómo una llama pequeña puede incendiar un bosque tan grande!
es.R: {{plural_you:Piénsenlo|Pensadlo}}: una llama muy pequeña puede quemar todo un bosque enorme.

sw.L: Tazama, moto mdogo namna gani unawasha msitu mkubwa namna gani!
sw.B: Tazama jinsi mwali mdogo unavyoweza kuunguza msitu mkubwa kiasi hicho!
sw.R: Fikirini jambo hili: mwali mdogo sana unaweza kuchoma msitu mzima mkubwa.

fr.L: Voyez quel petit feu enflamme quelle grande forêt !
fr.B: Voyez comme une petite flamme peut embraser une si grande forêt !
fr.R: Pensez-y : une toute petite flamme peut mettre le feu à toute une grande forêt.

ko.L: 보십시오, 얼마나 작은 불이 얼마나 큰 숲을 태웁니까!
ko.B: 보십시오, 아주 작은 불씨가 얼마나 큰 숲을 태워 버립니까!
ko.R: 생각해 보십시오. 작은 불씨 하나가 넓고 큰 숲을 다 태워 버릴 수 있습니다.

vi.L: Hãy xem ngọn lửa nhỏ dường nào đốt cháy khu rừng lớn dường nào!
vi.B: Hãy xem một ngọn lửa nhỏ có thể đốt cháy cả một khu rừng lớn biết bao!
vi.R: Hãy nghĩ xem. Một đốm lửa nhỏ xíu có thể đốt cháy cả một khu rừng rộng lớn.

pt.L: Vejam que fogo tão pequeno incendeia que floresta tão grande!
pt.B: Vejam como uma pequena chama pode pôr fogo numa floresta tão grande!
pt.R: Pensem nisto: uma chama bem pequena pode pôr fogo numa floresta enorme.

am.L: እነሆ፣ እንዴት ያለ ትንሽ እሳት እንዴት ያለውን ታላቅ ጫካ ያቃጥላል!
am.B: እንዴት ያለ ትንሽ ነበልባል እንዴት ያለውን ትልቅ ጫካ ሊያቃጥል እንደሚችል ተመልከቱ!
am.R: እስቲ አስቡት፤ ትንሽ ነበልባል ትልቅ ጫካን በሙሉ ሊያቃጥል ይችላል።

decisions.choice: how small ... how great: the same word in both senses
decisions.reason: ἡλίκος asks "how large?" and can point either way. James uses it twice, first for the small fire and then for the great forest, so the one word carries the contrast.

decisions.choice: forest: woodland or dry brush
decisions.reason: ὕλην can be timber, firewood or woodland. With "how great" it is a large stretch of wood or brush, the kind of land a summer fire could sweep through.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "how small a fire"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, including the text behind the King James Version, have a plain word for "little" in place of the first "how small". The meaning is the same; the SBLGNT reading keeps the play on one word (m1). This note is written from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: flame
decisions.reason: "Flame" says plainly that the fire is small at the start; "fire" returns in verse 6.

decisions.choice: "nhỏ dường nào ... lớn dường nào" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses one word for both "how small" and "how great" (m1). Literal repeats "dường nào" to keep the play.

source.text: καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα πῦρ, ὁ κόσμος τῆς ἀδικίας ἡ γλῶσσα καθίσταται ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν, ἡ σπιλοῦσα ὅλον τὸ σῶμα καὶ φλογίζουσα τὸν τροχὸν τῆς γενέσεως καὶ φλογιζομένη ὑπὸ τῆς γεέννης.

records.literal_gloss: And the tongue [is a] fire, the world of the unrighteousness the tongue is set among the members of us, the [one] staining whole the body and setting on fire the wheel of the existence and being set on fire by the Gehenna.

en.L: And the tongue [is] a fire. As the world of unrighteousness, the tongue is set among our members, staining the whole body and setting on fire the wheel of existence, and being set on fire by Gehenna.
en.B: And the tongue is a fire. It takes its place among the parts of our body as a world of wrongdoing: it stains the whole body, it sets the whole course of life on fire, and it is itself set on fire by hell.
en.R: The tongue is a fire too. It is a whole world of evil, there among the parts of our body. It stains the whole body. It sets the whole of life on fire, and its fire comes from hell.

es.L: Y la lengua [es] un fuego. Como el mundo de la injusticia, la lengua está puesta entre nuestros miembros, manchando todo el cuerpo y prendiendo fuego a la rueda de la existencia, y siendo encendida por la Gehena.
es.B: Y la lengua es un fuego. Entre las partes de nuestro cuerpo se presenta como todo un mundo de injusticia: mancha el cuerpo entero, incendia todo el curso de la vida, y ella misma es incendiada por el infierno.
es.R: La lengua también es un fuego. Está ahí, entre las partes de nuestro cuerpo, y es un mundo entero lleno de mal. Mancha todo el cuerpo. Prende fuego a toda la vida, y su fuego viene del infierno.

sw.L: Na ulimi [ni] moto. Kama ulimwengu wa udhalimu, ulimi umewekwa kati ya viungo vyetu, ukiutia doa mwili wote na kuliwasha moto gurudumu la maisha, na wenyewe ukiwashwa moto na Gehena.
sw.B: Ulimi nao ni moto. Umesimama kati ya viungo vya mwili wetu kama ulimwengu mzima wa udhalimu: unautia doa mwili wote, unawasha moto mwenendo mzima wa maisha, na wenyewe unawashwa moto na jehanamu.
sw.R: Ulimi pia ni moto. Ni ulimwengu mzima wa uovu, nao umo kati ya viungo vya mwili wetu. Unauchafua mwili wote. Unayawasha moto maisha yote ya mtu, na moto wake unatoka jehanamu.

fr.L: Et la langue [est] un feu. Comme le monde de l’injustice, la langue est établie parmi nos membres, souillant le corps tout entier et enflammant la roue de l’existence, et étant enflammée par la Géhenne.
fr.B: La langue aussi est un feu. Elle prend place parmi les membres de notre corps comme un monde de mal : elle souille le corps tout entier, elle enflamme tout le cours de la vie, et elle est elle-même enflammée par l’enfer.
fr.R: La langue est un feu, elle aussi. Elle est tout un monde de mal, là, parmi les parties de notre corps. Elle salit tout le corps. Elle met le feu à toute la vie, et son feu vient de l’enfer.

ko.L: 그리고 혀는 불입니다. 혀는 불의의 세계로서 우리 지체들 가운데 자리 잡고 있어, 온몸을 더럽히고 존재의 바퀴를 불사르며, 자신은 게헨나로부터 불이 붙습니다.
ko.B: 혀는 불입니다. 혀는 우리 몸의 지체들 가운데 자리 잡은 불의의 세계입니다. 혀는 온몸을 더럽히고, 삶의 모든 과정을 불태우며, 그 자신은 지옥 불에서 불이 붙습니다.
ko.R: 혀도 불과 같습니다. 혀는 우리 몸의 한 부분이지만, 그 안에는 온갖 악이 다 들어 있습니다. 혀는 온몸을 더럽힙니다. 혀는 사람의 온 삶을 불태웁니다. 그 불은 지옥에서 온 것입니다.

vi.L: Và cái lưỡi [là] một ngọn lửa. Là thế giới của sự bất chính, cái lưỡi được đặt giữa các chi thể chúng ta, làm ô uế cả thân thể, đốt cháy cả vòng xoay của cuộc đời, và chính nó bị Ghê-hen-na đốt cháy.
vi.B: Cái lưỡi cũng là một ngọn lửa. Nó chiếm chỗ giữa các bộ phận của thân thể chúng ta như cả một thế giới của điều gian ác: nó làm ô uế cả thân thể, đốt cháy cả dòng đời, và chính nó bị lửa địa ngục đốt cháy.
vi.R: Cái lưỡi cũng là một ngọn lửa. Nó là cả một thế giới của điều ác, nằm ngay giữa các bộ phận của thân thể chúng ta. Nó làm dơ bẩn cả thân thể. Nó đốt cháy cả cuộc đời con người, và lửa của nó đến từ địa ngục.

pt.L: E a língua [é] fogo. Como o mundo da injustiça, a língua está posta entre os nossos membros, contaminando o corpo inteiro e incendiando a roda da existência, e sendo incendiada pela geena.
pt.B: E a língua é um fogo. Ela ocupa o seu lugar entre as partes do nosso corpo como um mundo de maldade: mancha o corpo inteiro, põe fogo em todo o curso da vida e ela mesma é incendiada pelo inferno.
pt.R: A língua também é um fogo. Ela é um mundo inteiro de maldade, ali entre as partes do nosso corpo. Ela suja o corpo inteiro. Ela põe fogo na vida inteira, e o fogo dela vem do inferno.

am.L: ምላስም እሳት ነው፤ ምላስ የዓመፅ ዓለም ሆኖ በክፍሎቻችን መካከል ተቀምጧል፤ መላ ሰውነትን ያረክሳል፤ የሕልውናንም መንኮራኩር ያቃጥላል፤ እርሱም በገሃነም ይቃጠላል።
am.B: ምላስም እሳት ነው። በሰውነታችን ክፍሎች መካከል የክፋት ዓለም ሆኖ ይቀመጣል፤ መላ ሰውነትን ያረክሳል፤ የሕይወትን ሩጫ ሁሉ በእሳት ያቀጣጥላል፤ እርሱ ራሱም በገሃነም ይቀጣጠላል።
am.R: ምላስም እሳት ነው። በሰውነታችን ክፍሎች መካከል ያለ የክፋት ዓለም ነው። መላ ሰውነትን ያቆሽሻል። ሕይወትን ሁሉ በእሳት ያቃጥላል፤ እሳቱም የሚመጣው ከገሃነም ነው።

decisions.choice: the tongue is set among our members as the world of unrighteousness
alternatives: the tongue is a fire, a world of unrighteousness; the tongue is set among our members, staining ...
decisions.reason: The sentence is hard to divide. The SBLGNT puts a comma after πῦρ ("fire") and none after ἀδικίας, which makes "the world of unrighteousness" go with καθίσταται: among the parts of the body, the tongue stands as that world. Others join "world of unrighteousness" to "fire" and start a new clause at the second "the tongue". The meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: world: a whole realm, the sum of all wrongdoing in small
alternatives: an ornament (an old sense of the word)
decisions.reason: κόσμος usually means the world. Here "the world of unrighteousness" is the whole range of wrongdoing gathered into one small part of the body. It looks ahead to 4:4, where friendship with the world is enmity with God.

decisions.choice: the wheel of existence: the whole course of human life, from birth on
alternatives: the cycle of birth and death taught by some Greek religions
the course of the natural world
decisions.reason: τροχὸν is a wheel and γενέσεως is birth or existence (the same word as "natural face" in 1:23). The phrase was used in Greek writing for the round of life. James borrows it to say that the tongue can set a whole life burning, from beginning to end, not to teach anything about rebirth.

decisions.choice: Gehenna: the place of final judgment, and the power of evil behind it
decisions.reason: Gehenna was the Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem, where children had been burned in sacrifice (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31-32). Its name came to mean the place of final punishment, as in Jesus' words (Matthew 5:22; Mark 9:43). This is its only use outside the Gospels. The tongue's fire is lit from there: its destructive power comes from evil itself.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (Literal); hell (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name so the reader can see what James wrote; Balanced and Readable use the English word for what the name stands for (m4).

decisions.choice: unrighteousness (Literal); wrongdoing (Balanced); evil (Readable)
decisions.reason: ἀδικίας is the opposite of righteousness. Literal keeps the form; Balanced and Readable use plainer words for doing wrong.

decisions.choice: Gehena (L); jehanamu (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name, as the English does. "jehanamu", lowercase as in the NT terms table, is the word Swahili-speaking Christians use for hell, and it comes from the same name, so Balanced and Readable can say what the name stands for (m4) without losing it.

decisions.choice: la Géhenne (L); l’enfer (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English, Literal keeps the name of the place of final judgment (m4), with a capital as a proper name; Balanced and Readable say "l’enfer", the word French readers know for it.

decisions.choice: "게헨나" (L); "지옥" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean of Matthew 5:22-30: Literal keeps the name of the valley that stood for final judgment (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say "지옥", the word Korean readers know for it.

decisions.choice: "불의의 세계" (L, B); "존재의 바퀴" (L); "삶의 모든 과정" (B); "온 삶" (R)
alternatives: "불의의 세상", which would blur with "세상" for the world
decisions.reason: Here "world" means a whole realm of wrongdoing (meaning decision), not the world of 1:27 and 4:4, so Korean says "세계" rather than "세상". The wheel of existence is the whole course of life (meaning decision, uncertain); Literal keeps the picture, Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: "Ghê-hen-na" (L); "địa ngục" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Gehenna is the place of final judgment (m4). Literal gives the name James uses, in its Protestant transliteration; Balanced and Readable say "địa ngục", the Protestant word for hell, as the English says "hell". "Hỏa ngục" is the Catholic word.

decisions.choice: "thế giới" for "world" here, not "thế gian"
decisions.reason: The word here means a whole realm, all wrongdoing in small (m2), not the world set against God of 1:27 and 4:4. "Thế giới" says a complete world in itself and keeps "thế gian" for that other sense.

decisions.choice: ገሃነም (Gehenna) at every level
decisions.reason: "ገሃነም" is both the Greek word and the ordinary Amharic word for hell, so Balanced and Readable keep it where the English says "hell"; it is the word used for Gehenna in the Gospels.

source.text: πᾶσα γὰρ φύσις θηρίων τε καὶ πετεινῶν ἑρπετῶν τε καὶ ἐναλίων δαμάζεται καὶ δεδάμασται τῇ φύσει τῇ ἀνθρωπίνῃ·

records.literal_gloss: Every for kind of beasts both and birds, of reptiles both and sea creatures, is tamed and has been tamed by the nature the human;

en.L: For every kind of wild animals and birds, of reptiles and sea creatures, is being tamed and has been tamed by the human kind.
en.B: Every kind of wild animal and bird, of reptile and creature of the sea, is being tamed and has been tamed by humankind.
en.R: People can tame every kind of animal: wild animals, birds, reptiles and sea creatures. People have tamed them all.

es.L: Porque toda especie de fieras y de aves, de reptiles y de criaturas marinas, es domada y ha sido domada por la especie humana.
es.B: Toda clase de fieras y de aves, de reptiles y de animales del mar, se está domando y ha sido domada por el género humano.
es.R: La gente puede domar toda clase de animales: fieras, aves, reptiles y animales del mar. Los seres humanos los han domado a todos.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila aina ya wanyama wa porini na ndege, ya wanyama watambaao na viumbe vya baharini, inafugwa na imekwisha kufugwa na aina ya binadamu.
sw.B: Kila aina ya mnyama wa porini na ndege, ya mtambaazi na kiumbe cha baharini, inafugwa na imekwisha kufugwa na wanadamu.
sw.R: Watu wanaweza kufuga kila aina ya mnyama: wanyama wa porini, ndege, wanyama watambaao na viumbe vya baharini. Watu wamewafuga wote.

fr.L: Car toute espèce de bêtes sauvages et d’oiseaux, de reptiles et d’animaux marins, est domptée et a été domptée par l’espèce humaine.
fr.B: Toute espèce d’animaux sauvages et d’oiseaux, de reptiles et d’animaux marins, est domptée et a été domptée par l’espèce humaine.
fr.R: Les humains peuvent dompter toutes sortes d’animaux : les animaux sauvages, les oiseaux, les reptiles et les animaux de la mer. Ils les ont tous domptés.

ko.L: 들짐승과 새와 기는 것과 바다 생물의 모든 종류는 사람의 종류에게 길들여지고 있고, 또 길들여져 왔습니다.
ko.B: 온갖 종류의 짐승과 새와 파충류와 바다 생물을 사람이 길들이고 있고, 또 길들여 왔습니다.
ko.R: 사람은 온갖 동물을 길들일 수 있습니다. 들짐승도, 새도, 기어 다니는 동물도, 바다에 사는 동물도 길들입니다. 사람은 그것들을 다 길들여 왔습니다.

vi.L: Vì mọi loài thú vật và chim chóc, loài bò sát và loài sống dưới biển, đều đang bị và đã bị loài người chế ngự.
vi.B: Mọi loài thú rừng và chim chóc, bò sát và sinh vật dưới biển, đều đang được và đã được loài người thuần hóa.
vi.R: Con người có thể thuần hóa mọi loài vật: thú rừng, chim chóc, loài bò sát và các sinh vật dưới biển. Con người đã thuần hóa được tất cả.

pt.L: Pois toda espécie de feras e de aves, de répteis e de animais marinhos, é domada e tem sido domada pela espécie humana;
pt.B: Toda espécie de animal selvagem e de ave, de réptil e de criatura do mar, está sendo domada e já foi domada pela espécie humana.
pt.R: As pessoas conseguem domar todo tipo de animal: animais selvagens, aves, répteis e animais do mar. As pessoas já domaram todos eles.

am.L: የአራዊትና የወፎች፣ የተሳቢዎችና የባሕር ፍጥረታት ተፈጥሮ ሁሉ በሰው ተፈጥሮ ይገራልና፤ ተገርቷልምና።
am.B: የዱር አራዊትና የወፎች፣ የተሳቢዎችና የባሕር ፍጥረታት ዓይነት ሁሉ በሰው ልጅ ይገራል፤ ተገርቷልም።
am.R: ሰዎች ማንኛውንም ዓይነት እንስሳ መግራት ይችላሉ፤ የዱር አራዊትን፣ ወፎችን፣ ተሳቢዎችንና የባሕር ፍጥረታትን። ሰዎች ሁሉንም ገርተዋቸዋል።

decisions.choice: four kinds of creatures: an echo of Genesis
decisions.reason: Wild animals, birds, creeping things and creatures of the sea are the groups over which God gave humans rule (Genesis 1:26; 9:2; compare Psalm 8:8-9). Humans have done what they were made to do with every creature, but not with their own tongue (verse 8).

decisions.choice: kind ... human kind: the same word for animal and human nature
decisions.reason: φύσις is used twice: every "kind" of creature is tamed by the human "kind". The repetition sets humanity over against all other creatures.

decisions.choice: is being tamed and has been tamed: an ongoing work, and a done one
decisions.reason: The present δαμάζεται says it goes on; the perfect δεδάμασται says it has been achieved. Both make the contrast in verse 8 sharper.

decisions.choice: People can tame ...; People have tamed them all.
alternatives: Every kind ... is being tamed and has been tamed by humankind
decisions.reason: Readable makes "people" the subject and gives the two verbs a sentence each.

decisions.choice: toda especie ... la especie humana
decisions.reason: Literal uses one word, "especie", for both uses of φύσις, so the reader sees the repetition that sets humankind over the other creatures (m2). "Naturaleza" would also repeat, but "toda naturaleza de fieras" is no longer natural Spanish.

decisions.choice: kufuga
decisions.reason: "Kufuga" is to tame and keep animals, the everyday word for what people do with them; "kutiisha" (to subdue) would echo Genesis 1:28 but says less about taming. Literal also repeats "aina" for both uses of φύσις (m2).

decisions.choice: espèce ... l’espèce humaine (L, B)
decisions.reason: James uses the same word for every kind of animal and for humankind (m2). French "espèce" works for both and is inclusive, so Literal and Balanced keep the repeated word.

decisions.choice: "모든 종류 ... 사람의 종류" (L)
decisions.reason: The same Greek word stands for animal kinds and for humankind (meaning decision); Literal repeats "종류" so the reader sees it, and Balanced and Readable say "사람".

decisions.choice: "loài" for both "kind" and "humankind" ("loài người")
decisions.reason: James uses one word for the kind of animal and for human kind (m2). Vietnamese "loài" does the same in "loài thú" and "loài người", so the echo stays at every level; "loài người" needs no gender span.

decisions.choice: espécie ... espécie humana
decisions.reason: Portuguese "espécie" can stand for both uses of the one Greek word, so the repetition m2 points to is kept: every species is tamed by the human species.

source.text: τὴν δὲ γλῶσσαν οὐδεὶς δαμάσαι δύναται ἀνθρώπων· ἀκατάστατον κακόν, μεστὴ ἰοῦ θανατηφόρου.

records.literal_gloss: But the tongue no one to tame is able of men; a restless evil, full of poison deadly.

en.L: But no one of {{gender:people|men}} is able to tame the tongue: a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
en.B: But no human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
en.R: But no one can tame the tongue. It is evil, and it never rests. It is full of poison that kills.

es.L: Pero la lengua, ninguno de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} es capaz de domarla: [es] un mal inquieto, llena de veneno mortal.
es.B: Pero ningún ser humano puede domar la lengua. Es un mal que nunca se está quieto, y está llena de un veneno mortífero.
es.R: Pero nadie puede domar la lengua. Es mala y nunca descansa. Está llena de un veneno que mata.

sw.L: Lakini ulimi hakuna mtu kati ya wanadamu anayeweza kuufuga: [ni] uovu usio na utulivu, uliojaa sumu ya kuua.
sw.B: Lakini hakuna binadamu anayeweza kuufuga ulimi. Ni uovu usiotulia kamwe, na umejaa sumu inayoleta kifo.
sw.R: Lakini hakuna mtu anayeweza kuufuga ulimi. Ni mbaya, na hautulii kamwe. Umejaa sumu inayoua.

fr.L: Mais la langue, aucun des {{gender:humains|hommes}} ne peut la dompter : [c’est] un mal sans repos, plein d’un venin mortel.
fr.B: Mais la langue, aucun être humain ne peut la dompter. C’est un mal qui ne connaît pas de repos, plein d’un venin mortel.
fr.R: Mais personne ne peut dompter la langue. Elle est mauvaise, et elle ne se repose jamais. Elle est pleine d’un poison qui tue.

ko.L: 그러나 사람들 가운데 아무도 혀는 길들일 수 없습니다. [혀는] 쉬지 않는 악이요, 죽이는 독으로 가득합니다.
ko.B: 그러나 혀는 아무도 길들일 수 없습니다. 혀는 쉬지 않고 날뛰는 악이며, 죽음을 가져오는 독으로 가득합니다.

vi.L: Nhưng cái lưỡi thì không ai trong loài người có thể chế ngự được: [nó là] điều ác không yên nghỉ, đầy chất độc chết người.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "restless"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, including the text behind the King James Version, have a similar word meaning "that cannot be restrained". The SBLGNT reads ἀκατάστατον, "restless, unstable". The sense is close. This note is written from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: restless: unstable, never at rest
decisions.reason: ἀκατάστατος is the word for the double-minded man in 1:8, and its noun returns in verse 16 ("disorder"). The tongue is like a wild animal that cannot be kept still.

decisions.choice: full of deadly poison: the poison of the serpent
decisions.reason: The psalm says of the wicked, "the poison of vipers is under their lips" (Psalm 140:4), and Paul quotes it of human speech (Romans 3:13). Like a snake, the tongue can kill.

decisions.choice: no one of people: no human being, by human power
alternatives: no one at all can, not even God
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων sets the tongue against verse 7: humans tame every creature but not this. James does not say God cannot; his call to receive wisdom from God (1:5; 3:17) assumes help comes from above.

decisions.choice: "사람들 가운데 아무도" (L) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The word means human beings (meaning decision); Korean "사람" already includes men and women.

source.text: ἐν αὐτῇ εὐλογοῦμεν τὸν κύριον καὶ πατέρα, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ καταρώμεθα τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς καθ’ ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ γεγονότας·

records.literal_gloss: With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse the men the [ones] according to likeness of God having been made;

en.L: With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse {{gender:people|men}}, who have been made according to the likeness of God.

en.R: We use our tongues to praise God, our Lord and Father. Then we use them to curse people, and God made those people to be like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

sw.B: Kwa ulimi tunambariki Bwana na Baba, na kwa ulimi huohuo tunawalaani wanadamu, ambao wameumbwa wakifanana na Mungu.

ko.L: 우리는 그것으로 주님이시며 아버지이신 분을 찬양하고, 또 그것으로 하나님의 모양대로 지음 받은 사람들을 저주합니다.

pt.L: Com ela bendizemos o Senhor e Pai, e com ela amaldiçoamos {{gender:os seres humanos|os homens}}, que foram feitos segundo a semelhança de Deus.
pt.B: Com a língua bendizemos o Senhor e Pai, e com ela amaldiçoamos os seres humanos, que foram feitos à semelhança de Deus.
pt.R: Usamos a língua para louvar a Deus, o nosso Senhor e Pai. Depois a usamos para amaldiçoar as pessoas, e Deus fez essas pessoas para serem parecidas com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

am.L: በእርሱ ጌታንና አባትን እንባርካለን፤ በእርሱም በእግዚአብሔር አምሳል የተፈጠሩትን ሰዎች እንረግማለን።
am.B: በምላሳችን ጌታና አባት የሆነውን እግዚአብሔርን እንባርካለን፤ በዚያው ምላስ በእግዚአብሔር አምሳል የተፈጠሩትን ሰዎች እንረግማለን።
am.R: በምላሳችን ጌታችንና አባታችን የሆነውን እግዚአብሔርን እናወድሳለን። ከዚያም በዚያው ምላሳችን ሰዎችን እንረግማለን፤ እነዚያን ሰዎች ግን እግዚአብሔር እርሱን እንዲመስሉ አድርጎ ፈጥሯቸዋል።

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the Lord and Father"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, including the text behind the King James Version, read "God" in place of "Lord". The SBLGNT reading "the Lord and Father" is found only here in the New Testament. The one meant is the same. This note is written from general knowledge and must be checked against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Lord and Father: God, named with one article as both
alternatives: the Lord Jesus and the Father
decisions.reason: One article governs both words, so they name one person: God, who is Lord and Father (compare "God and Father" in 1:27).

decisions.choice: made according to the likeness of God: Genesis 1:26
decisions.reason: ὁμοίωσιν is the word of Genesis 1:26 in the Greek Old Testament: "let us make humankind ... according to our likeness". The perfect γεγονότας says people still bear that likeness. To curse a person is to curse what bears God's likeness, so blessing God and cursing people with one tongue cannot fit together (Genesis 9:6).

decisions.choice: bless and curse: words spoken to God and against people
decisions.reason: To bless God is to praise him; Jewish prayers began "Blessed be God" (as Luke 1:68; 2 Corinthians 1:3). To curse a person was to call down harm on them. Both are acts of speech, the tongue's best and worst.

decisions.choice: praise God, our Lord and Father
decisions.reason: Readable says "praise" for blessing God (m4) and names God, so a young reader knows who is meant (m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Readable turns "the likeness of God" into "to be like him"; the pronoun is for God.

decisions.choice: {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: "Los seres humanos" is chosen over "las personas" so that the relative clause that follows ("que han llegado a ser") agrees with either reading of the setting.

decisions.choice: tunambariki Bwana
decisions.reason: Swahili "kubariki" can take God as its object, as in the prayer "Tumbariki Bwana", and it keeps James's pair blessing and cursing ("baraka" and "laana" in verse 10). "Kuhimidi" (to praise) is the other common word; Readable uses "kusifu" as the English Readable uses "praise". A reviewer may prefer "kuhimidi".

decisions.choice: les {{gender:humains|hommes}} (L); des êtres humains (B); des gens (R)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 2:8: Literal needs a noun for human beings and carries the setting; Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "찬양하다" for bless (God), "저주하다" for curse
decisions.reason: When God is the one blessed, the word means praise (meaning decision); Korean "축복하다" is said of blessing people, so "찬양하다" is used. The noun in verse 10 is "찬양".

decisions.choice: "chúc tụng" and "nguyền rủa" (L, B); "ca ngợi" (R)
decisions.reason: To bless God is to speak his praise (m4); "chúc tụng" is said of God, "chúc phước" of people. Readable says "ca ngợi", as the English Readable says "praise".

decisions.choice: {{gender:os seres humanos|os homens}}
decisions.reason: "Seres humanos" is masculine in grammar, so "feitos" agrees with both options; with "as pessoas" the participle would also have to go inside the span.

es.B: Bendición y maldición salen de la misma boca.

vi.R: Lời ca ngợi và lời nguyền rủa ra từ cùng một cái miệng.

pt.L: Da mesma boca saem bênção e maldição.
pt.B: Bênção e maldição saem da mesma boca.
pt.R: Louvor e maldições saem da mesma boca.

decisions.choice: blessing and cursing: words that call for good and for harm

decisions.choice: praise
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, Readable uses "praise" for the blessing of God.

source.text: οὐ χρή, ἀδελφοί μου, ταῦτα οὕτως γίνεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: Not it is fitting, brothers of me, these things so to happen.

en.B: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, it must not be this way.
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, this is wrong. It should not happen.

es.B: Hermanos míos, no es correcto que esto suceda así.

sw.L: Haipasi, ndugu zangu, mambo haya yatokee hivyo.
sw.B: Ndugu zangu, jambo hili halipaswi kuwa hivi.
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, jambo hili ni baya. Halipaswi kutokea.

fr.B: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, il ne doit pas en être ainsi.
fr.R: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, c’est mal. Cela ne devrait pas arriver.

ko.B: 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 이래서는 안 됩니다.
ko.R: 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 이것은 잘못된 일입니다. 이런 일이 있어서는 안 됩니다.

vi.L: Không nên, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, những điều này xảy ra như vậy.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, không được như thế.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, điều này là sai. Không nên để nó xảy ra.

pt.L: Não convém, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, que essas coisas sejam assim.
pt.B: Meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, não pode ser assim.
pt.R: Meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, isso está errado. Não deveria acontecer.

am.L: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ ይህ እንዲህ ሊሆን አይገባም።
am.B: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ ይህ እንዲህ መሆን የለበትም።
am.R: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ ይህ ስሕተት ነው። መሆን የለበትም።

decisions.choice: my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Gender setting: James addresses the whole congregation, women and men.

es.R: El agua dulce y el agua amarga no salen del mismo manantial, ¿verdad?
